chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh ibn Nusayr, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid and others, they said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
May Allah have mercy on Zurara ibn A'yan; if it were not for Zurara and his peers, the narrations of my father would have perished.

key_terms.أَحَادِيثُ أَبِي: The narrations of my father (referring to Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir)
key_terms.زُرَارَةُ بْنُ أَعْيَنَ: Zurara ibn A'yan, a prominent companion of the Imams known for his role in transmitting hadith
key_terms.نَظِيرُهُ: His peers/equivalents, referring to other key narrators of the same era

ai.seo_question: Why is Zurara ibn A'yan considered crucial for the preservation of Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights Zurara ibn A'yan as the preeminent narrator among the Shi'a, asserting that without his rigorous scholarship and those like him, the authentic traditions of the Imams would have been lost. This statement underscores the critical role of individual reliability (thiqa) in the transmission of Shia jurisprudence and establishes Zurara as a foundational pillar of the Hadith corpus.

en.ammaar-muslim: 6. [6/-] Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh b. Nusayr from Ya’qub b. Yazid and Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi al-Khattab from Muhammad b. Abi Umayr from Ibrahim b. Abd al-Hamid and others apart from him – they all said: Abu Abdillah عليه السلام said:
may Allah have mercy on Zurara bin A’yan, if it was not for Zurara b. A’yan and his peers the narrations of my father would have perished.
